text:
mike: Heads up — billing alarm: GPU OOD (on-demand) spend spiked ~+42% over the last 2h. Alert tied to mass autoscale launches in eu-central-1. Seeing a lot of eu nodes with no commitment tag.
sara: Ack. I just pulled the allocation logs — autoscaler launched 27 g4dn/g5a equivalents in eu-central instead of our committed pools in us-west.
jess: That matches what I saw in the provisioner: a recent policy change added `preferred_zone: eu-*` and it ended up taking precedence over the commitment label. Looks like label precedence logic regressed.
tom: Wait — we have reserved commitments scoped to the committed_pool label. Autoscaler should prefer committed_pool first. Was there a change to fallback order?
mike: Yes — fallback order got reordered in last week's rollout: preferred_zone -> cheapest -> committed_pool. That explains it. The string match for preferred_zone also accidentally matched eu-central when preference was intended for colocated test racks.
sara: Oof. So the autoscaler intentionally honored zone affinity, but ignored reservation coverage. Result: launched expensive on-demand GPUs outside commitment scope.
jess: Quick mitigation: I pushed a hotfix to revert the precedence to `committed_pool` -> `preferred_zone` and added an explicit `nodeSelector: committed_pool=true` for production GPU workloads. PR: https://git.internal/infra/pull/824
devops-bot: Deploy started: autoscaler/patch-commitment-first (build 2026-03-18_09:12) :rocket:
mike: Great — can we also roll a temporary admission rule to block launches in non-committed regions for prod GPU node groups until the fix is live?
tom: Added temporary admission webhook. It rejects provisioner requests if `workload=prod-gpu` and `committed_pool!=true`.
finance: We've flagged the excess charges with cloud billing team. Rough estimate ~ $19.6k overrun so far. Opening a billing inquiry ticket.
sara: Monitoring shows new launches are now landing in committed pools only. Commitment hit-rate metric jumped back to ~98%.
jess: Postmortem action items: 1) E2E test for label precedence 2) metric for `commitment_hit_rate` and alert if <90% 3) revert risky fallback rollouts behind experiment flag.
mike: Agreed. Also update runbook to include a quick jira checklist for commitment mismatches and who to ping in finance.
devops-bot: Incident annotation: root_cause=autoscaler_fallback_reorder; impact=on-demand_gpu_spend; estimated_cost=19600; status=mitigated
finance: I'll follow up with procurement on whether we can recoup some overages under our cloud commitments policy.
tom: I've scheduled a short postmortem doc and assigned owners. Will drop link here when ready.
mike: Thanks all. Keeping this thread open for one more hour to watch billing window, then I'll collapse and circulate summary to eng leads. :thumbsup:
